response.title: which robot mower leaves the fewest missed patches
response.answer:
If your top priority is a robot lawn mower that leaves the fewest uncut patches, I'd focus on navigation accuracy, systematic mowing patterns, and obstacle avoidance—not just cutting power.

The biggest differences are:

Coverage consistency: Does it mow in precise, overlapping rows rather than wandering randomly?

Obstacle handling: Does it return to areas it skipped around trees, furniture, and garden beds?

Edge cutting: How much grass remains along fences, walls, and borders?

Positioning reliability: Can it maintain accurate navigation under trees and near buildings?

A mower can have excellent navigation yet still leave strips along edges because its blade cannot physically reach them.

My top 3 choices for minimizing missed grass
Shop
My first choice

Mammotion LUBA 3 AWD

Best for complex lawns, trees, slopes, and irregular areas. Combines LiDAR, RTK positioning, and cameras. Independent tests report excellent cut consistency and navigation, although automatic mapping can initially miss sections. 
Bob Vila
+1

Shop

Segway Navimow X430

Best for precise, systematic coverage on larger lawns. It received 5/5 for cut quality and performance in Bob Vila's testing, with accurate boundaries and reliable navigation. 
Bob Vila

Shop

Ecovacs GOAT A3000 LiDAR PRO

Best candidate when missed grass along edges is the main concern. Its LiDAR navigation and dedicated edge-trimming system make it especially interesting for lawns bordered by fences or walls. 
Bob Vila

$2,499.99 at Best Buy

Important caveat: There isn't a trustworthy standardized test measuring the percentage of lawn missed by every model, so I wouldn't claim any one mower has a proven lowest missed-patch rate.

Random uncut strips in open lawn

Along fences, walls, and lawn edges
Under trees or near buildings where GPS is weak
